source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ τὰ ἅγια, εἰς λόγον εὐλογιῶν, κατὰ τὴν ἑορτὴν τοῦ Πάσχα, εἰς ἑτέρας παροικίας διαπέμπεσθαι. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Συνήθεια ἦτο εἰς τοὺς παλαιοὺς να πέμπουσιν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τοῦ Πάσχα τὰ θεία Μυστήρια ἀπὸ μίαν ἐπαρχίαν εἰς ἄλλην, χάριν εὐλογίας καὶ ἁγιασμοῦ ἐκείνων, πρὸς τοὺς ὁποίους ἐστέλλοντο(2), τὴν ὁποίαν συνήθειαν ἐμποδίζει ὁ παρών Κανών, ἐπειδὴ εἶναι ἀπρεπὲς νά περιφέρωνται τὰ πάντιμᾳ Μυστήρια εἰς μακρὰς ὁδοιπορίας ἁπλῶς καὶ ὡς ἔτυχε.
thought_title: No sending the holy gifts as blessings at Pascha
orientation: The council is issuing its canons; this one forbids a custom of sending the consecrated eucharistic gifts from one parish to another at Pascha as a blessing.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the [matter] not the holy [things], for [the] purpose of blessings, according to the feast of the Pascha, to other parishes to be sent. Interpretation. A custom it was among the ancients that they send in the time of the Pascha the divine Mysteries from one province to another, for [the] sake of blessing and sanctification of those, to whom they were sent, which custom hinders the present Canon, since it is improper that they be carried around the all-precious Mysteries on long journeys simply and as it happened.

lemmas.gloss: to send across, send from one place to another
to be carried about, borne around

choices.why: The source uses the neuter plural substantive for the consecrated eucharistic elements; 'holy things' preserves the literal force without adding a noun.
The phrase means 'for the purpose of blessings' or 'as blessings'; 'by way of blessings' keeps the literal sense of λόγος as manner or purpose.
The source uses the technical term Μυστήρια for the consecrated eucharistic elements; capitalizing 'Mysteries' signals the technical sense.
The phrase means 'casually and haphazardly'; the literal rendering preserves the two adverbial expressions of carelessness.

pass_b_english: Concerning the holy things not being sent across to other parishes by way of blessings at the feast of Pascha. Interpretation. It was a custom among the ancients to send the divine Mysteries at the time of Pascha from one province to another, for the blessing and sanctification of those to whom they were sent. This custom the present canon hinders, because it is improper for the all-honored Mysteries to be carried about on long journeys simply and as it happened.
